Subtopic: Responsible AI state of the field
Title: Responsible AI | The 2026 AI Index Report
What it covers: Tracks AI incidents, safety evaluation, transparency, responsible-AI reporting, and the widening gap between capability and governance.
Why the reader benefits: Best current snapshot for showing that AI capability is advancing faster than safety measurement and transparency.
Best use: Lecture opener; literature review motivation; 2026 statistics
Key ethical question: Are current evaluation and governance systems keeping pace with frontier AI capability?
Notes / status: 2026 edition; strong source for current facts and figures.

Title: The 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index
What it covers: Scores major foundation-model developers on disclosures covering data, compute, risk mitigation, usage and downstream impacts.
Why the reader benefits: Lets readers move from vague calls for transparency to measurable disclosure dimensions and compare developers.
Best use: Transparency section; accountability case study; assignment
Key ethical question: What information should frontier-model developers be required to disclose?
Notes / status: Average score fell from 58/100 in 2024 to 40/100 in 2025.

Title: AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future
What it covers: Official overview of the EU AI Act, risk-based obligations, implementation timeline, GPAI rules and transparency requirements.
Why the reader benefits: Provides the clearest bridge between ethics principles and enforceable legal duties in 2026.
Best use: Regulation module; compliance discussion; policy comparison
Key ethical question: When should ethical expectations become legal obligations?
Notes / status: General application date: 2 August 2026, with exceptions and phased provisions.

Title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems
What it covers: Explains Article 50 duties concerning user disclosure, machine-readable marking, AI-generated content and deepfakes.
Why the reader benefits: Useful concrete example of how transparency ethics becomes a product-design requirement.
Key ethical question: Should people always know when they are interacting with AI or seeing AI-generated content?

Title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models
What it covers: Clarifies obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models and the Commission's enforcement role.
Why the reader benefits: Gives readers a current compliance perspective on frontier and general-purpose models rather than generic AI regulation.
Best use: GPAI governance; provider responsibilities; seminar discussion
Key ethical question: What extra duties should apply to powerful general-purpose models?
Notes / status: Commission enforcement powers apply from 2 August 2026.

Title: India AI Governance Guidelines: Empowering Ethical and Responsible AI
What it covers: Sets out principles and recommendations around fairness, accountability, safety, inclusivity and trustworthy AI in India.
Why the reader benefits: Adds an India-specific governance perspective and prevents the reading list from being US/EU-centric.
Best use: India case study; policy comparison; local context
Key ethical question: How should responsible AI governance reflect India's scale diversity and public-interest priorities?
Notes / status: Released 5 Nov 2025 under the IndiaAI Mission.

Title: Safe & Trusted AI Working Group
What it covers: Focuses on AI safety capacity, evaluation, governance and incorporating Global South perspectives into international AI safety frameworks.
Why the reader benefits: Useful for understanding how safety debates are being localized beyond US/EU institutions.
Best use: India 2026 update; global governance; discussion prompt
Key ethical question: Who gets to define acceptable AI risk and safety standards globally?

Title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
What it covers: Identifies GenAI-specific risks and actions across the AI lifecycle, aligned with Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.
Why the reader benefits: One of the most practical sources for converting ethical concerns into operational risk controls.
Best use: Risk register; deployment checklist; governance design
Key ethical question: How can an organization operationalize trustworthy GenAI rather than merely state principles?

Title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
What it covers: Defines principles including proportionality, do-no-harm, safety, privacy, fairness, transparency, accountability, sustainability and human oversight.
Why the reader benefits: Provides a normative foundation for almost every later AI ethics topic.
Best use: Foundations lecture; ethics framework; compare policies
Key ethical question: What values should guide the design and deployment of AI systems?
Notes / status: Global UNESCO recommendation; remains foundational in 2026.

Title: OECD AI Principles
What it covers: Principles for innovative and trustworthy AI, covering human rights, fairness, transparency, robustness, security and accountability.
Why the reader benefits: Concise policy baseline that is easy to compare against NIST UNESCO EU and national frameworks.
Best use: Framework comparison; policy lecture; exam preparation
Key ethical question: What minimum principles should trustworthy AI systems satisfy across countries?
